headline: Racing's leaky defence meets winless Espanyol at El Sardinero
summary: Two clubs level on 8 points meet at El Sardinero, and the market can barely split them: Racing Santander are 39.8% favourites, Espanyol 33.9%. The puzzle is Racing's defence, which has conceded chances worth 3.26 expected goals per game, more than double Espanyol's 1.27. Espanyol's problem is at the other end: they lost their last game 0-1 to Atletico Madrid and are four league games without a win. Yassir Zabiri, with 7 goals, is Racing's main threat. The handicap is level — home advantage is the one difference — and the goals line sits at 2.75.
read: Both sides sit on eight points in the lower half, and the market makes Racing Santander narrow home favourites at 39.8% with the handicap level. Racing have been conceding chances at 3.26 xG a game — more than double Espanyol's rate — but Espanyol arrive four matches without a win, so the market sees a close mid-table scrap with goals in it.

facts.fact: Racing Santander are the narrow home favourites at 39.8%, with Espanyol at 33.9% and the draw at 26.3%.
facts.meaning: A close game in the market's eyes — home advantage is doing most of the separating, not a quality gap.

facts.fact: Racing Santander have conceded chances worth 3.26 xG per game across their last five matches.
facts.meaning: They give up clear chances almost every week, which is why their games have been high-scoring and their goal difference is so poor.

facts.fact: Espanyol's last five league results read L-D-L-L-W: one win in five and four games without a win.
facts.meaning: They arrive short of form and short of goals, which is why the market still makes the home side favourite.

facts.fact: Racing Santander's goal difference is -12 after nine games, against Espanyol's -1.
facts.meaning: Their defeats have been heavy rather than narrow — the season numbers are the worst of the two, yet the price treats them as slight favourites.

facts.fact: Espanyol lost 0-1 at home to Atletico Madrid on 17 October, Alex Baena scoring in the 89th minute.
facts.meaning: They were in the game to the last minute against one of the league's strongest sides — their defeats have been decided by small margins.

facts.fact: The total-goals line sits at 2.75, with over priced at 52.2%.
facts.meaning: The market leans, more likely than not, towards three goals or more at El Sardinero.

facts.fact: Racing Santander's win chance has moved from 38.2% to 39.8% in recent days, with Espanyol dropping from 35.4% to 33.9%.
facts.meaning: A small but one-directional shift towards the home side on the outright market.

facts.fact: Yassir Zabiri has scored seven goals in eight La Liga appearances for Racing Santander this season.
facts.meaning: He is the main threat in a side that otherwise creates little — Racing have scored six in five matches as a team.

sources.fact: Spanish media report that Racing Santander defender Pedro Felipe left training early with a knock three days before the Espanyol match and his availability is in doubt.
Pedro Felipe has played only 76 minutes across three La Liga appearances this season, all off the bench.
Yassir Zabiri has scored seven goals in eight La Liga appearances for Racing Santander this season, against an expected-goals total of just 3.3.
Goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala made five saves in Racing Santander's most recent match but conceded the only goals of the game.
Inigo Vicente delivered accurate crosses for Racing Santander in their last match but could not create a clear goalscoring chance.
Espanyol are 16th in La Liga with eight points from nine games, just one point above the relegation zone, and have gone four matches without a win.
Espanyol lost 1-0 at home to Atletico Madrid, with Alex Baena scoring the winner in the 89th minute.
Espanyol are playing their 90th season in Spain's top flight, and only four clubs have spent more seasons in La Liga.
